task: Horizon 09 of agent-agnostic-browser-bridge. Horizon 08 added an evalIsolated chrome-bridge action to read values on strict-CSP sites via an isolated-world string eval; live testing proved this impossible (MV3's extension CSP forbids eval in every world). The only route to strict-CSP value reads is CDP Runtime.evaluate, previously barred by decisions.md (h6 + h8). The user has decided to lift that ban for read-only page evaluation (and greenlight the broader CDP pivot for later horizons) and to remove the dead evalIsolated action. This horizon: remove evalIsolated, add a CDP Runtime.evaluate port, wire a new evaluatePage action end to end, and verify strict-CSP value reads in live Chrome.

analysis.objective: Lift the project's ban on CDP Runtime.evaluate for read-only page evaluation, ship a CDP-backed evaluatePage action that reads values from strict-CSP sites, and remove the non-functional evalIsolated action it replaces.
analysis.successDefinition: npm run verify is green for tools/chrome-bridge with evalIsolated fully removed; a new evaluatePage action calls CDP Runtime.evaluate on the sandbox tab; a live-Chrome transcript shows evaluatePage returning a real value on at least two strict-CSP sites while executeScript still returns the page's CSP error on the same expression; executeScript's own behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged.
assumptions: chrome.debugger.sendCommand supports Runtime.evaluate with returnByValue + awaitPromise from an MV3 service worker (the debugger permission is already granted and already used for Page.captureScreenshot).

CDP Runtime.evaluate is exempt from the page's Content-Security-Policy (it is the documented DevTools mechanism; executeScript's CSP failure is specific to chrome.scripting, per horizon-04 discoveries).
The dedicated sandbox tab remains the sole action target (horizon-06 decision); evaluatePage resolves it the same way every other action does.
A live-Chrome check can be run this horizon via the chrome-bridge MCP; if it cannot, phase 4 ends blocked with MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING and exact retry steps rather than done-but-unverified.
risks: CDP Runtime.evaluate could itself hit a Trusted-Types or site-specific restriction on some target — mitigated by phase 4 testing at least two strict-CSP sites head-to-head against executeScript.

Sharing the attach/detach lifecycle between captureScreenshot and evaluate could regress screenshot capture if the refactor is careless — mitigated by an explicit unchanged-behaviour rubric dimension.
Attaching chrome.debugger raises Chrome's 'started debugging this browser' banner on the sandbox tab — acceptable because the tab is deliberately kept unfocused, but noted.
outOfScope: Trusted synthetic input via CDP Input.dispatch* — greenlit by the horizon-09 decision but not built this horizon; no phase needs it.
CDP-driven scroll and virtualized-list materialization — deferred to a later horizon now that the CDP door is open.
Persistent multi-command CDP sessions (vs per-command attach/detach) — deferred until a phase actually needs session continuity.
Removing or deprecating executeScript now that CDP eval is a functional superset — executeScript stays unchanged this horizon.
DOM page-model snapshot / findElement-refs (horizon-05, never executed) — still deferred.
Deleting the deliberately-dead active-tab surface — still deferred.
Relocating the result-size cap to a generic MCP-layer truncation — evaluatePage reuses the existing per-action cap.
analysis.domainShapeReason: Developer tooling — a Chrome extension, a chrome.debugger/CDP adapter and an MCP tool catalog; no business entities or rules a domain expert would recognize.

ubiquitousLanguage.meaning: The low-level Chrome control protocol reached from the extension via chrome.debugger; not subject to a page's Content-Security-Policy.
The CDP command that evaluates a JavaScript expression in a tab's page context and returns its value.
One discrete capability listed in PAGE_ACTIONS and exposed as exactly one MCP tool.
The single auto-created background tab that every page action targets since horizon 06.
A site whose Content-Security-Policy blocks chrome.scripting eval — github.com, reddit.com, LinkedIn.
The horizon-08 action being removed; it attempted isolated-world string eval, which MV3 forbids in every world.
The chrome.debugger-backed port module (formerly CaptureDebuggerPorts) that owns the attach / send-command / detach lifecycle with leak-safe cleanup.

discoveryFindings.finding: tools/chrome-bridge/src/extension/debugger-ports.ts already implements attach -> single CDP command -> detach with an onDetach listener and an inFlight map that rejects only the interrupted capture, registered once at construction. It exposes only captureScreenshot(tabId).
discoveryFindings.implication: Runtime.evaluate is the same attach/command/detach lifecycle; add it as a second method on this module and factor out the shared attach/cleanup rather than duplicating it.

discoveryFindings.finding: createPageActionHandlers(ports, sandboxTab, captureDebugger) — every handler does `const tabId = await sandboxTab.resolveTabId()`; captureTab already delegates to captureDebugger.captureScreenshot(tabId). guard() wraps each handler in the guarded return map.
discoveryFindings.implication: evaluatePage's handler is a 4-line body: resolve sandbox tab, call captureDebugger.evaluate(tabId, code), coerce the outcome. No new constructor parameter needed.

discoveryFindings.finding: executeScript and evalIsolated both return an in-page `InPageScriptOutcome` ({ ok, json } | { ok: false, error }) that coerceExecuteScriptOutcome maps to { result: { value } } | { error }, with a MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS (1_000_000) cap applied handler-side.
discoveryFindings.implication: The CDP evaluate method should return the same InPageScriptOutcome shape so the handler reuses coerceExecuteScriptOutcome unchanged; the size cap stays where it is.

discoveryFindings.finding: Adding a page action requires edits in six coordinated places: PAGE_ACTIONS tuple, PageActionParams + PageActionResults mapped types (plus the two named interfaces), the raw handler map, the guarded return map, TOOL_CATALOG, and the count-hardcoded unit tests (actions.unit.test.ts, tool-catalog.unit.test.ts). All are typed Record<PageAction, ...> so a missing one is a tsc error.
discoveryFindings.implication: Phase 3 is one type-locked atomic unit that must land with its count tests; phase 1's removal and phase 3's addition each touch the same six places.

discoveryFindings.finding: evalIsolated appears in exactly these files: actions.ts (tuple), actions.unit.test.ts (tuple + count 18), types.ts (2 interfaces + 2 map entries), page-actions.ts (raw handler ~453-508 + guarded map line 620), page-actions.unit.test.ts (describe block ~1036-1160), tool-catalog.ts (line 212), tool-catalog.unit.test.ts (line 45 + count), README.md (lines 51, ~199, 217, plus the 'eighteen page actions'/'18 tools' counts).
discoveryFindings.implication: Removal is fully enumerable and small; grep for evalIsolated / EvalIsolated must return zero hits when phase 1 is done.

discoveryFindings.finding: A newly added page action is only callable after the chrome-bridge MCP server restarts (it advertises its tool list at startup) AND dist/extension is rebuilt and the unpacked extension is remove+re-added. A stale service worker makes a new action silently TIME OUT (isCommand() drops the frame) rather than returning an 'unknown action' error.
discoveryFindings.implication: Phase 4 must rebuild, restart the MCP server, and remove+re-add the extension before testing; the failure signature to distinguish stale-build from a real hang is 'timeout, never an unknown-action error'.

discoveryFindings.finding: On github.com (script-src, no unsafe-eval) and reddit.com (script-src 'self' 'strict-dynamic' nonce, no unsafe-eval), executeScript returns Chrome's verbatim CSP-eval error, not a value. On the sandbox tab, evalIsolated returned the extension's OWN MV3 CSP error — proving no string-eval world exists.
discoveryFindings.implication: Phase 4's head-to-head is well-grounded: executeScript is the known-failing control, evaluatePage via CDP is the treatment; github.com + one of reddit/LinkedIn are the target sites.

phases.name: Remove the non-functional evalIsolated action
phases.goal: Delete the evalIsolated page action and its entire protocol / handler / catalog / test / documentation surface, returning PAGE_ACTIONS to 17 entries with npm run verify green.
phases.rationale: Horizon 08 shipped an 'evalIsolated' MCP tool meant to read values on strict-CSP sites by running a caller-supplied string through JavaScript's eval inside the extension's isolated content-script world. Live testing proved this can never work: Chrome's MV3 platform forbids string evaluation in every execution world, including the isolated one, because the extension's own Content-Security-Policy disallows it and MV3 does not let that policy be relaxed. Every call to the tool returns a CSP error. A permanently-dead tool advertised in the MCP catalog misleads any AI agent connected to the bridge into believing the capability exists, so it is removed rather than left frozen.
phases.rationaleTerms: MV3 = Manifest V3, the current Chrome extension platform. Content-Security-Policy (CSP) = a browser rule set restricting which code a page (or extension) may execute. Isolated world = the private JavaScript context a content script runs in, separate from the page's own scripts.

Remove evalIsolated from the README action enumeration (two spots) and its manual e2e step; change the 'eighteen page actions' / 'connected with 18 tools' counts to seventeen / 17.

phases.name: Add a CDP port that reads page values
phases.goal: Add an evaluate(tabId, expression) method to the chrome.debugger-backed port module that runs an expression against a tab through CDP Runtime.evaluate and returns a JSON-serialisable value or an error, reusing the module's existing attach / detach / leak-cleanup lifecycle.
phases.rationale: The chrome-bridge extension can already drive a Chrome DevTools Protocol session against the dedicated background sandbox tab — horizon 06 added debugger-ports.ts, which attaches a debugger, runs one CDP command, and detaches, with cleanup so a crash never leaks the attachment. That module today exposes only screenshot capture. CDP's Runtime.evaluate command evaluates a JavaScript expression in the page's real context and is not subject to any Content-Security-Policy — it is the one mechanism that can read values from strict-CSP sites like LinkedIn, github.com and reddit, where the existing executeScript action is blocked. This phase adds that one CDP call as a new port method; wiring it into a user-facing action is the next phase.
phases.rationaleTerms: Port = a small interface isolating one slice of the chrome.* API so it can be faked in tests. Runtime.evaluate params: returnByValue asks CDP to send back the value itself (not a remote handle); awaitPromise resolves a returned promise before replying.
changes: Rename the CaptureDebuggerPorts interface to DebuggerPorts (it is no longer capture-only) and update its single importer in page-actions.ts; keep captureScreenshot and add evaluate(tabId: number, expression: string): Promise<InPageScriptOutcome>.

Factor the shared attach / inFlight-registration / onDetach / detach-in-finally machinery out of captureScreenshot into a private helper both methods call, so captureScreenshot's observable behaviour does not change.
Implement evaluate: attach, sendCommand({ tabId }, "Runtime.evaluate", { expression, returnByValue: true, awaitPromise: true }), detach in finally.

Map the CDP reply to InPageScriptOutcome: exceptionDetails present -> { ok: false, error: exceptionDetails.exception?.description ?? exceptionDetails.text }; otherwise JSON.stringify(result.value), apply the same MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS cap the executeScript handler uses (export the constant from page-actions.ts or move it to a shared module), and return { ok: true, json }; undefined / non-serialisable value -> the same error strings executeScript returns.

Add co-located unit tests with a stubbed chrome.debugger: successful value read, exceptionDetails -> error, over-large value -> cap error, detach runs on the error path, no attachment leak after either path.
inputs: The existing attach/detach/onDetach/inFlight pattern in debugger-ports.ts.
CDP Runtime.evaluate parameter semantics (returnByValue, awaitPromise, exceptionDetails).
phases.expectedResult: DebuggerPorts.evaluate exists with a co-located unit test covering each exported behaviour (per the testguard rule for *-ports.ts files), npm run verify is green, and captureScreenshot's behaviour is unchanged (the diff is additive plus a behaviour-preserving extraction of the shared attach helper).

rubric.label: evaluate runs through CDP Runtime.evaluate
rubric.ruleStatement: The method issues chrome.debugger sendCommand for Runtime.evaluate with returnByValue and awaitPromise, not chrome.scripting or any string-eval, so it is exempt from page CSP by construction.
passCriteria: The implementation calls sendCommand({tabId}, 'Runtime.evaluate', { expression, returnByValue: true, awaitPromise: true })
No chrome.scripting.executeScript and no eval/new Function appear in the method
A unit test asserts the exact CDP command name and params object
failureExamples: awaitPromise is omitted, so `await fetch(...)` style expressions return a pending Promise serialised as {}
returnByValue is omitted, so result.value is undefined and the method returns an unhelpful empty read on every call

rubric.label: Returns the same outcome shape and size cap as executeScript
rubric.ruleStatement: evaluate returns InPageScriptOutcome ({ ok, json } | { ok: false, error }); CDP exceptionDetails become an error; a value over MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS becomes the same cap error the executeScript handler produces.
passCriteria: The handler in the next phase can call coerceExecuteScriptOutcome on the result with no adaptation
exceptionDetails -> { ok: false, error } with a message drawn from the exception
an over-large stringified value -> { ok: false, error } matching the executeScript cap wording
the shared constant is imported/moved, not re-hardcoded to a different number
failureExamples: exceptionDetails is ignored and a thrown page expression resolves as { ok: true, json: 'undefined' }
the size cap is silently dropped so a 5 MB DOM dump is returned and blows the MCP response

rubric.label: captureScreenshot still works after the refactor
rubric.ruleStatement: Extracting the shared attach/detach/leak-cleanup helper does not change captureScreenshot's observable behaviour, including its onDetach rejection and its detach-in-finally.
passCriteria: Existing captureScreenshot unit tests pass unchanged
the onDetach listener is still registered once, not per call
both methods detach on every path including error
failureExamples: The shared helper registers a fresh onDetach listener per call, leaking listeners across many evaluate calls
evaluate's error path returns before detach, leaving the sandbox tab attached and showing the debugging banner permanently

rubric.label: Co-located unit test per exported behaviour
rubric.ruleStatement: debugger-ports.unit.test.ts covers evaluate's success, exception, over-large, and detach-on-error paths with a stubbed chrome.debugger, satisfying the testguard rule for *-ports.ts files.
passCriteria: Each of the four paths has an assertion
the test stubs chrome.debugger and never touches a real browser
the coverage guard passes for the changed file
failureExamples: Only the happy path is tested; the exceptionDetails mapping ships unverified
the test asserts the method was called but not what CDP command it issued

phases.healerHint: If a dimension fails, check that awaitPromise + returnByValue are both set and exceptionDetails is mapped to an error; the screenshot regression is nearly always a per-call onDetach listener — register it once in the shared helper.
phases.compensation: None — additive infrastructure with no external effect; revert the phase's commit to remove it.

phases.name: Add the evaluatePage action end to end
phases.goal: Wire a new evaluatePage page action through the protocol tuple, param/result types, raw + guarded handler (calling DebuggerPorts.evaluate on the sandbox tab), TOOL_CATALOG entry, and count-hardcoded tests, bringing PAGE_ACTIONS to 18.
phases.rationale: With the CDP Runtime.evaluate port method in place (previous phase) and the dead evalIsolated removed (first phase), the bridge needs a user-facing MCP tool that an AI agent calls to read a value from a strict-CSP page. This follows the exact 'add one page action' shape the project has used seven times: one entry in the single source-of-truth tuple, a named params interface ({ code: string }) and result interface ({ value?: unknown; error?: string }), a handler in both the raw and guarded maps, one TOOL_CATALOG description with required: ['code'], and tests that hardcode the new action count. The handler resolves the dedicated sandbox tab (like every action since horizon 06) and delegates to the CDP port.
phases.rationaleTerms: Raw handler map vs guarded return map = the extension defines each handler once, then wraps every one in a guard() that catches throws and normalizes errors before returning; both maps are typed Record<PageAction, Handler> so a missing key fails the type-check.
changes: Add "evaluatePage" to the PAGE_ACTIONS tuple, immediately after "executeScript".

Add EvaluatePageParams { readonly code: string } and EvaluatePageResult { readonly value?: unknown; readonly error?: string } interfaces plus their entries in the PageActionParams and PageActionResults mapped types.

Add the raw evaluatePage handler: reject a non-string / empty code with { error }, `const tabId = await sandboxTab.resolveTabId()`, `const outcome = await captureDebugger.evaluate(tabId, params.code)`, `return coerceExecuteScriptOutcome(outcome)`; add it to the guarded return map as `evaluatePage: guard(raw.evaluatePage)`.

Add TOOL_CATALOG.evaluatePage: description says it evaluates an expression against the real page via Chrome DevTools Protocol and works on strict-CSP sites where executeScript is blocked; inputSchema { code: string }, required: ['code'].

Update the ordered-tuple assertion and hardcoded counts to 18 in actions.unit.test.ts and tool-catalog.unit.test.ts; add handler tests in page-actions.unit.test.ts (value read, empty/missing code, port-returned error passthrough) using a fake captureDebugger.evaluate.
README: add evaluatePage to the action enumeration (two spots), bump the counts to eighteen / 18, and add a manual e2e step describing a strict-CSP read.
inputs: The PAGE_ACTIONS tuple and the PageActionParams / PageActionResults mapped types.
The createPageActionHandlers(ports, sandboxTab, captureDebugger) signature and coerceExecuteScriptOutcome.
The TOOL_CATALOG Record<PageAction, ToolCatalogEntry> shape and the two count-hardcoded test files.
phases.expectedResult: npm run verify green; evaluatePage present in PAGE_ACTIONS (length 18), both mapped types, both handler maps, and TOOL_CATALOG; the MCP server's listTools derives 18 tools; git diff shows the executeScript handler, its unit block, and coerceExecuteScriptOutcome / MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS untouched.

rubric.label: The action is wired in every one of the six coordinated places

grep of the diff shows zero @ts-ignore / @ts-expect-error / as any / as unknown escapes
the count-hardcoded tests assert 18 and name evaluatePage in the ordered tuple

rubric.label: The handler resolves the sandbox tab and delegates to the CDP port
rubric.ruleStatement: evaluatePage validates code is a non-empty string, resolves the tab via sandboxTab.resolveTabId(), calls captureDebugger.evaluate(tabId, code), and returns coerceExecuteScriptOutcome(outcome) — no new coercion logic.
passCriteria: Unit tests: a value read returns { result: { value } }; empty/missing code returns { error } before any port call; a port-returned { ok: false, error } passes straight through
the handler body reuses coerceExecuteScriptOutcome, not a hand-rolled mapper
the guarded map entry is evaluatePage: guard(raw.evaluatePage)

rubric.label: executeScript is byte-for-byte unchanged
rubric.ruleStatement: The git diff adds evaluatePage without editing the executeScript handler, its unit block, its TOOL_CATALOG description, or the shared coerceExecuteScriptOutcome / MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS helpers.
passCriteria: git diff on page-actions.ts is additive for executeScript's lines

rubric.label: The tool description tells an agent when to use it
rubric.ruleStatement: TOOL_CATALOG.evaluatePage states that it evaluates an expression against the real page via Chrome DevTools Protocol and works on strict-CSP sites where executeScript is blocked, and that it reads (does not reliably mutate) page state.
passCriteria: The description names CDP and the strict-CSP use case
it does not over-claim trusted input or mutation
README's enumeration and counts are updated to eighteen / 18

phases.healerHint: If parity fails it is a missed one of the six places — add the key, do not cast; if the handler dimension fails, delete any executeScript/MAIN fallback and delegate purely to captureDebugger.evaluate.
phases.compensation: Revert this phase's commit to remove the evaluatePage surface if the CDP approach is abandoned.

phases.name: Verify strict-CSP value reads in live Chrome
phases.goal: Prove evaluatePage returns a real value from a strict-CSP site in a live signed-in Chrome via the chrome-bridge MCP, head-to-head with executeScript still failing on the same expression, and record the result.
phases.rationale: Every horizon that changes the extension closes with a real-Chrome end-to-end check rather than shipping done-but-unverified — a binding project decision from horizon 02. Horizon 08's premise died precisely because this check was left for last and then failed; running it here is what keeps horizon 09 honest. The check confirms that CDP Runtime.evaluate is genuinely CSP-exempt in practice, not just in theory.
phases.rationaleTerms: Head-to-head = calling both actions with the same expression on the same tab, so any difference is attributable to the CDP-vs-chrome.scripting path and nothing else.
changes: Rebuild dist/extension; restart the chrome-bridge MCP server so it advertises evaluatePage; remove + re-add the unpacked extension in chrome://extensions (a stale service worker makes a new action time out silently).

Via the chrome-bridge MCP: navigateTo https://github.com; getTabState to confirm the sandbox tab anchored; evaluatePage { code: "document.querySelector('h1')?.innerText" } -> expect a string value; executeScript with the same code -> expect github.com's page-CSP error.
Repeat the evaluatePage read on one of reddit.com or LinkedIn (signed in).
Record the measured transcript in README's manual-verification list and as a one-line discoveries.md entry; mark the two horizon-08 evalIsolated blockers resolved in blockers.md.
If the live check cannot be run in-session, end the phase blocked with MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING and the exact rebuild + reload + retry steps.
inputs: The chrome-bridge MCP running against real signed-in Chrome.
The stale-service-worker reload procedure (remove + re-add dist/extension) from horizon-07 discoveries.
The strict-CSP site evidence for github.com and reddit.com from horizon-04 discoveries.
phases.expectedResult: A recorded live transcript showing evaluatePage returning a non-error value on at least two strict-CSP sites and executeScript still returning the page's CSP error on the same expression; the outcome written to README and discoveries.md. If unrunnable in-session, a blocked row with MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING and precise retry steps — never done-but-unverified.
